newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao to face forgery charges in court.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao to face forgery charges in court.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao will appear in court on Wednesday to face forgery charges in a seven-year-old criminal case, his lawyer said on Tuesday.
R.K. Anand told Reuters that Rao would appear at a hearing set for 10 a.m. (0430 GMT) in a high-security courtroom in an international conference centre in the Indian capital.
"I am bringing him," Anand told Reuters.

Rao would be the first former or serving prime minister to appear in court to face criminal charges. Former prime minister Indira Gandhi was summoned to court after the Emergency ended in 1977 in a civil case.

Hundreds of journalists were expected to converge on the cavernous Vigyan Bhavan centre, chosen by police as a replacement site for crowded local courts where they feared an attack on the 75-year-old former prime minister.

Rao had been scheduled to appear in court in September. But two cases -- one involving alleged forgery, the other criminal conspiracy to cheat -- bogged down in procedural manoeuvres, and Rao has been spared the humiliation of either a court appearance or being taken into custoy.
Rao served as prime minister from 1991 until last May when his Congress party, hobbled by accusations of corruption, suffered a humiliating defeat in general elections.
He stepped down as Congress leader in September after a local judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in the criminal cheating case.
But Rao, who said he was innocent of the charge of cheating a businessman out of $100,000 in 1983, has remained leader of Congress's parliamentary delegation and still has political clout.
His influence is magnified by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's dependence on the Congress party's support to help thwart potential challenges from right-wing Hindu nationalists in parliament.
Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coalition does not control an outright majority in the lower house of parliament, and needs Congress's backing.
Anand said that at Wednesday's hearing, his team would press chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar to extend the temporary bail that has protected Rao from arrest but which expires on November 6.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, on September 26 charged Rao and three others with involvement in an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
Rao has not commented publicly on the case.
Rao has been named but not formally charged in the 1983 cheating case. Both the forgery and cheating cases carry maximum penalties of seven years in jail.
The CBI has also named Rao in a vote-buying case which is still under investigation.

Lawmakers of the regional Jharkand Mukti Morcha party said they were paid $100,000 to vote against a 1993 no-confidence motion which Rao's Congress-led government survived by a wafer-thin margin. Rao has denied any wrongdoing.
